NEW FILENAMES, NOT THE v4 NAMES. Shopify SUFFIXES rather than replaces on a name collision, so re-uploading `skingenetix-review-model-pdrn-serum-2026-v4.jpg` would leave the OLD image being served and quietly add a `_1` twin. The three old files are therefore left untouched on the CDN and only the block's `image` setting is repointed — which is also shopify.md rule 7, since translations key off the URL. The old files stay live and reusable; nothing is deleted.

THE NEW NAMES ARE ALSO BETTER SEO THAN THE ONES THEY REPLACE. `...-2026-v4` spends two of its words on a revision number that no shopper will ever type, and `check_seo_name()` flags both `v4` and a bare `2026` as carrying no search value. The new names lead with the product a shopper would search for and then describe the picture. `acetyl-hexapeptide-8` will still trip the bare-digit warning on its `8`; that is a false positive - the 8 is part of the ingredient's actual name and is worth keeping.

WEB-READY MEANS RE-ENCODED, NOT JUST RESIZED. The three masters are 4096x4096 PNGs at ~9.4MB each. `upload-theme-images.py` caps the long edge at 3000 (the widest the theme's srcset ever requests), re-encodes to progressive JPEG at q95 4:4:4, and strips EXIF/ICC. Quality stays HIGH deliberately: Shopify's CDN transcodes to WebP per breakpoint, so the uploaded JPEG is never what a visitor downloads, and pre-compressing it just hands the WebP encoder a picture full of artefacts. Measured on this store: a q85 source delivered MORE bytes at every width than a q93 one.

⚠️ COLOUR-TO-PRODUCT MISMATCH ON review_4, FLAGGED TO MALCOLM. The light-blue cream is the Copper Peptide NIGHT cream #A6C4E0. The slide it now sits on is headed by a Glutathione review and its button reads 'Shop Glutathione Brightening Serum' - and the Glutathione serum is a completely transparent, untinted liquid. So that slide shows a blue cream while selling a colourless serum. review_2 is a near-miss of the same kind but defensible: the pink cream is the PDRN Collagen Repair CREAM #F3BFC2 while the slide sells the PDRN Renewal SERUM, whose own substance is a translucent rose-pink - both are pink, so the picture does not contradict the product. review_6 is an exact match: Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 is one of the three transparent serums. Malcolm chose these having seen the sheet; nothing is blocked on it, but if the carousel should be substance-accurate then review_4 wants the clear-serum frame and the light blue belongs on a Copper Peptide Night Cream slide.

The alt text describes what is actually in each photograph rather than the product being sold, which is both correct for accessibility and keeps the review_4 discrepancy visible instead of papering over it. No woman is described as a customer or a trial participant.
